cards.front: Which artery supplies each part of the embryonic gut (foregut, midgut, hindgut), and where does each part end?
cards.back: **Foregut** (**celiac trunk**): to the proximal duodenum, at the major papilla. **Midgut** (**SMA**): distal duodenum to the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon. **Hindgut** (**IMA**): distal third of the transverse colon to the anal canal above the **pectinate line**.
cards.back_pt: **Intestino anterior** (**tronco celíaco**): até o duodeno proximal, na papila maior. **Intestino médio** (**AMS**): duodeno distal até os dois terços proximais do cólon transverso. **Intestino posterior** (**AMI**): terço distal do cólon transverso até o canal anal acima da **linha pectínea**.

cards.front: Which two colon regions are watershed areas, and why are they at risk in hypotension?
cards.back: The **splenic flexure** (border between **SMA** and **IMA** territories) and the **rectosigmoid junction** (border between the last sigmoid branch and the **superior rectal** artery). They sit at the ends of two arterial beds, so low flow causes **ischemic colitis** there first.
cards.back_pt: A **flexura esplênica** (limite entre os territórios da **AMS** e da **AMI**) e a **junção retossigmoide** (limite entre o último ramo sigmoide e a artéria **retal superior**). Ficam no fim de dois leitos arteriais, então o fluxo baixo causa **colite isquêmica** primeiro ali.

cards.front: How does the midgut normally develop, and what can go wrong in malrotation?
cards.back: The midgut **herniates** into the umbilical cord at about **week 6**, turns **270° counterclockwise** around the **SMA**, and returns by about **week 10**. **Malrotation**: high cecum, **Ladd bands** over the duodenum, and risk of **midgut volvulus**.
cards.back_pt: O intestino médio **hernia** para o cordão umbilical por volta da **6ª semana**, gira **270° no sentido anti-horário** em torno da **AMS** e retorna por volta da **10ª semana**. **Má rotação**: ceco alto, **bandas de Ladd** sobre o duodeno e risco de **volvo de intestino médio**.

cards.front: What is a Meckel diverticulum, and why can it bleed?
cards.back: A **true diverticulum** (all wall layers) of the ileum, left when the **vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct** fails to obliterate. It may contain ectopic **gastric** or pancreatic tissue. Acid from gastric mucosa ulcerates nearby ileum and causes **painless rectal bleeding** in a young child.
cards.back_pt: **Divertículo verdadeiro** (todas as camadas da parede) do íleo, resultante da falha de obliteração do **ducto vitelino (onfalomesentérico)**. Pode conter tecido **gástrico** ou pancreático ectópico. O ácido da mucosa gástrica ulcera o íleo vizinho e causa **sangramento retal indolor** em criança pequena.

cards.front: What is the developmental defect in Hirschsprung disease?
cards.back: **Neural crest cells** fail to migrate to the distal colon, so the **rectum** and a variable continuous segment above it lack ganglion cells in both plexuses. The segment cannot relax. Linked to **RET** mutations and **Down syndrome**. Diagnosis: **rectal suction biopsy**.
cards.back_pt: As **células da crista neural** não migram até o cólon distal, então o **reto** e um segmento contínuo variável acima dele não têm células ganglionares nos dois plexos. O segmento não relaxa. Associada a mutações do **RET** e à **síndrome de Down**. Diagnóstico: **biópsia retal por sucção**.

cards.front: How do annular pancreas and pancreas divisum arise?
cards.back: **Annular pancreas**: the **ventral pancreatic bud** forms a ring around the **second part of the duodenum** and can obstruct it. **Pancreas divisum**: the ventral and dorsal **ducts fail to fuse**; most drainage goes through the **minor papilla**. Divisum is usually asymptomatic.
cards.back_pt: **Pâncreas anular**: o **broto pancreático ventral** forma um anel em torno da **segunda porção do duodeno** e pode obstruí-la. **Pâncreas divisum**: os **ductos** ventral e dorsal **não se fundem**; a maior parte da drenagem ocorre pela **papila menor**. O divisum geralmente é assintomático.

cards.front: In portal hypertension, which portal and systemic veins connect at the esophagus, umbilicus and rectum?
cards.back: **Esophagus**: left gastric ↔ esophageal veins (to azygos) → **esophageal varices**. **Umbilicus**: paraumbilical ↔ **epigastric veins** of the abdominal wall → **caput medusae**. **Rectum**: superior rectal ↔ middle and inferior rectal veins → **anorectal varices**.
cards.back_pt: **Esôfago**: gástrica esquerda ↔ veias esofágicas (para a ázigos) → **varizes esofágicas**. **Umbigo**: paraumbilicais ↔ **veias epigástricas** da parede abdominal → **cabeça de medusa** (*caput medusae*). **Reto**: retal superior ↔ retais média e inferior → **varizes anorretais**.

cards.front: What runs in the hepatoduodenal ligament, and what does the Pringle maneuver do?
cards.back: It holds the **portal triad**: **proper hepatic artery**, **portal vein** and **common bile duct**. It forms the front edge of the **epiploic foramen (of Winslow)**, which joins the greater and lesser sacs. The **Pringle maneuver** clamps it to stop hepatic inflow during liver bleeding.
cards.back_pt: Contém a **tríade portal**: **artéria hepática própria**, **veia porta** e **ducto colédoco**. Forma a borda anterior do **forame epiploico (de Winslow)**, que une a cavidade peritoneal maior à bolsa omental. A **manobra de Pringle** o clampeia para interromper o influxo hepático no sangramento do fígado.

questions.stem: A newborn girl starts vomiting green fluid a few hours after her first feed. She vomits after every feed. The pregnancy was complicated by polyhydramnios. She has upslanting palpebral fissures, a flat facial profile and a single palmar crease on each hand. The abdomen is not distended. An abdominal x-ray shows two large air bubbles in the upper abdomen and no gas in the rest of the bowel. Which developmental error most likely explains her vomiting?
choices: Ladd bands from incomplete rotation of the midgut
Failure of neural crest cells to migrate to the distal colon
Failure of the duodenal lumen to recanalize
Hypertrophy of the pyloric smooth muscle
Persistence of the vitelline duct
questions.explanation: This is **duodenal atresia**, which is strongly linked to **Down syndrome**. The duodenal lumen is temporarily solid and normally **recanalizes**; when it does not, air fills the stomach and proximal duodenum (**double bubble**) with **no distal gas**, and swallowed amniotic fluid cannot reach the distal bowel to be absorbed (polyhydramnios). **Malrotation** also causes bilious vomiting, but it often leaves some gas beyond the duodenum and is not the classic Down syndrome lesion. Pyloric stenosis causes nonbilious vomiting and appears weeks after birth.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **atresia duodenal**, fortemente associada à **síndrome de Down**. A luz duodenal fica temporariamente sólida e normalmente se **recanaliza**; quando isso não ocorre, o ar enche o estômago e o duodeno proximal (**sinal da dupla bolha**) **sem gás distal**, e o líquido amniótico deglutido não chega ao intestino distal para ser absorvido (polidrâmnio). A **má rotação** também causa vômitos biliosos, mas costuma deixar algum gás além do duodeno e não é a lesão clássica da síndrome de Down. A estenose hipertrófica do piloro causa vômitos não biliosos e surge semanas após o nascimento.

questions.stem: A 5-week-old boy, the first child of his parents, has had forceful vomiting after every feed for 4 days. The vomit is milky and never green. He seems hungry right after vomiting. He has fewer wet diapers than before, and his mucous membranes are dry. Visible waves of peristalsis move across the upper abdomen from left to right, and a firm, mobile, olive-sized mass is felt in the epigastrium. Which set of serum findings is most likely?
choices: High anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperkalemia
Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperchloremia
Respiratory alkalosis with normal chloride
Metabolic acidosis with hypokalemia and hypochloremia
Metabolic alkalosis with hypochloremia and hypokalemia
questions.explanation: **Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis** blocks gastric outflow, so the infant loses **HCl** in vomit. Loss of acid and chloride causes **hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis**, and volume depletion activates **aldosterone**, which wastes potassium in the urine (**hypokalemia**). Dehydration could suggest a metabolic acidosis, but gastric acid loss dominates; acidosis appears only with severe, late dehydration. Bile-free vomit fits an obstruction above the ampulla.
questions.explanation_pt: A **estenose hipertrófica do piloro** bloqueia o esvaziamento gástrico, e o lactente perde **HCl** no vômito. A perda de ácido e de **cloreto** causa **alcalose metabólica hipoclorêmica**, e a hipovolemia ativa a **aldosterona**, que elimina potássio na urina (**hipocalemia**). A desidratação poderia sugerir acidose metabólica, mas a perda de ácido gástrico predomina; a acidose só surge na desidratação grave e tardia. O vômito sem bile é compatível com obstrução proximal à ampola de Vater.

questions.stem: A term newborn boy has a large midline defect at the umbilicus. Loops of bowel and part of the liver lie inside a thin, translucent membrane, and the umbilical cord inserts into the top of this sac. Echocardiography shows a ventricular septal defect. Which developmental error most likely explains the abdominal wall finding?
choices: Failure of the physiologically herniated abdominal contents to return to the abdominal cavity
Full-thickness defect of the abdominal wall to the right of the umbilical cord
Incomplete obliteration of the vitelline duct
Incomplete closure of the umbilical ring after birth
Persistence of the allantois as a patent urachus
questions.explanation: This is an **omphalocele**: abdominal contents stay in the base of the umbilical cord instead of returning to the abdomen, so they are **covered by a membrane** of peritoneum and amnion and the defect is **midline**. Omphalocele is often linked to **other anomalies**, such as heart defects, chromosomal trisomies and Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. **Gastroschisis** is the tempting distractor, but it lies beside the cord (usually on the right), has **no covering sac**, and is rarely linked to other anomalies.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **onfalocele**: o conteúdo abdominal permanece na base do cordão umbilical em vez de retornar ao abdome, então fica **coberto por uma membrana** de peritônio e âmnio e o defeito é **mediano**. A onfalocele é frequentemente associada a **outras anomalias**, como cardiopatias, trissomias e síndrome de Beckwith-Wiedemann. A **gastrosquise** é o distrator tentador, mas fica ao lado do cordão (geralmente à direita), **não tem saco** de cobertura e raramente se associa a outras anomalias.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man has a bulge in the right groin that has grown over 1 year. It gets bigger when he stands or coughs and disappears when he lies down. It does not extend into the scrotum. During surgical repair, the hernia sac pushes forward through the posterior wall of the inguinal canal, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. Which mechanism best explains this hernia?
choices: Patent processus vaginalis
Weakness of the transversalis fascia in the inguinal (Hesselbach) triangle
Enlargement of the femoral ring below the inguinal ligament
Defect in the linea alba above the umbilicus
Incomplete closure of the umbilical ring
questions.explanation: A sac **medial to the inferior epigastric vessels** that bulges through the floor of the inguinal canal is a **direct inguinal hernia**. It comes from acquired **weakness of the transversalis fascia** in the inguinal (Hesselbach) triangle and is typical of older men. A **patent processus vaginalis** causes an **indirect** hernia, which enters the deep inguinal ring **lateral** to the inferior epigastric vessels and can descend into the scrotum. A femoral hernia lies below the inguinal ligament.
questions.explanation_pt: Um saco **medial aos vasos epigástricos inferiores** que abaula pelo assoalho do canal inguinal é uma **hérnia inguinal direta**. Ela decorre de **fraqueza adquirida da fáscia transversal** no triângulo inguinal (de Hesselbach) e é típica de homens idosos. Um **processo vaginal pérvio** causa hérnia **indireta**, que entra pelo anel inguinal profundo **lateralmente** aos vasos epigástricos inferiores e pode descer até o escroto. A hérnia femoral fica abaixo do ligamento inguinal.

notes.title: GI anatomy and embryology: gut regions, defects and key anatomy
notes.body_md:
## Gut regions and arteries

- **Foregut** (**celiac trunk**): esophagus to the major duodenal papilla, plus liver, gallbladder and most of the pancreas.
- **Midgut** (**SMA**): rest of the duodenum to the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon.
- **Hindgut** (**IMA**): distal third of the transverse colon to the pectinate line.
- **Watershed areas**: **splenic flexure** and **rectosigmoid junction**.

## Midgut and abdominal wall

- Physiologic herniation into the cord, **270° counterclockwise** rotation around the SMA, then return.
- **Malrotation**: Ladd bands, **midgut volvulus**, bilious vomiting.
- **Omphalocele**: midline, **covered sac**, often other anomalies.
- **Gastroschisis**: beside the cord, **no sac**, usually isolated.

## Obstruction and bleeding in infants

- **Duodenal atresia**: failed recanalization, **double bubble**, Down syndrome.
- **Pyloric stenosis**: about weeks 2-6, projectile **nonbilious** vomiting, olive mass, **hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis**.
- **Hirschsprung disease**: failed **neural crest** migration, aganglionic rectum, delayed meconium, **RET**.
- **Meckel diverticulum**: vitelline duct remnant; ectopic gastric mucosa causes painless bleeding.

## Pancreas

- **Annular pancreas**: ventral bud rings the duodenum.
- **Pancreas divisum**: ducts do not fuse.

## Peritoneum

- **Retroperitoneal**: most of the duodenum, pancreas (not the tail), ascending and descending colon, kidneys, adrenals, aorta, IVC, ureters, esophagus and lower rectum.
- **Hepatoduodenal ligament**: hepatic artery, portal vein, common bile duct; bounds the **epiploic foramen**.

## Gut wall

- **Meissner** (submucosal) plexus: secretion and local blood flow.
- **Auerbach** (myenteric) plexus: motility, between the muscle layers.
- **Brunner glands**: duodenal submucosa, alkaline mucus.
- **Peyer patches**: ileum, lymphoid tissue with M cells.

## Hernias and portal collaterals

- **Indirect**: lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, patent processus vaginalis.
- **Direct**: medial, through Hesselbach triangle.
- **Portal-systemic sites**: esophagus, umbilicus (**caput medusae**), rectum, retroperitoneum.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Regiões do intestino e artérias

- **Intestino anterior** (**tronco celíaco**): do esôfago até a papila duodenal maior, além de fígado, vesícula biliar e maior parte do pâncreas.
- **Intestino médio** (**AMS**): restante do duodeno até os dois terços proximais do cólon transverso.
- **Intestino posterior** (**AMI**): terço distal do cólon transverso até a linha pectínea.
- **Áreas de transição vascular** (*watershed*): **flexura esplênica** e **junção retossigmoide**.

## Intestino médio e parede abdominal

- Herniação fisiológica para o cordão, rotação de **270° em sentido anti-horário** em torno da AMS e retorno.
- **Má rotação**: bandas de Ladd, **volvo de intestino médio**, vômitos biliosos.
- **Onfalocele**: mediana, **coberta por saco**, frequentemente com outras anomalias.
- **Gastrosquise**: ao lado do cordão, **sem saco**, geralmente isolada.

## Obstrução e sangramento no lactente

- **Atresia duodenal**: falha de recanalização, **dupla bolha**, síndrome de Down.
- **Estenose hipertrófica do piloro**: cerca de 2-6 semanas, vômitos em jato **não biliosos**, massa em oliva, **alcalose metabólica hipoclorêmica e hipocalêmica**.
- **Doença de Hirschsprung**: falha de migração da **crista neural**, reto aganglionar, atraso na eliminação de mecônio, **RET**.
- **Divertículo de Meckel**: resquício do ducto vitelino; mucosa gástrica ectópica causa sangramento indolor.

## Pâncreas

- **Pâncreas anular**: o broto ventral forma um anel em torno do duodeno.
- **Pâncreas divisum**: os ductos não se fundem.

## Peritônio

- **Retroperitoneais**: maior parte do duodeno, pâncreas (exceto a cauda), cólons ascendente e descendente, rins, adrenais, aorta, VCI, ureteres, esôfago e reto inferior.
- **Ligamento hepatoduodenal**: artéria hepática, veia porta, colédoco; delimita o **forame epiploico**.

## Parede intestinal

- Plexo de **Meissner** (submucoso): secreção e fluxo sanguíneo local.
- Plexo de **Auerbach** (mioentérico): motilidade, entre as camadas musculares.
- **Glândulas de Brunner**: submucosa duodenal, muco alcalino.
- **Placas de Peyer**: íleo, tecido linfoide com células M.

## Hérnias e colaterais portais

- **Indireta**: lateral aos vasos epigástricos inferiores, processo vaginal pérvio.
- **Direta**: medial, pelo triângulo de Hesselbach.
- **Locais de anastomose portossistêmica**: esôfago, umbigo (**cabeça de medusa**), reto, retroperitônio.
